value: Industrial AI company whose sensors and software watch the health of factory machines, diagnosing problems early so plants avoid unplanned downtime.

Tractian installs its own sensors on industrial machinery, capturing data such as vibration, temperature and electrical current, and its AI models analyse that data to predict failures and guide maintenance. The sensors are provided to customers on loan and Tractian earns recurring revenue from the service. It reports more than 2,000 factories as customers and annualised recurring revenue of nearly US$100 million in 2026.

The company calls itself 'the asset health company'; its product predicts machine failures.

value: AI financial assistant for small businesses and self-employed people that runs inside WhatsApp and its own app, handling payments, charges and money management by text, voice or photo.

Jota is a Brazilian fintech that gives micro-entrepreneurs a digital account and an AI assistant inside WhatsApp, where they pay, charge via Pix or card, and ask about their finances. It reports about 300,000 clients and R$3.5 billion in annualised payment volume. Monetisation comes from acquiring (the FalaTap phone card reader) and receivables advance, with credit planned.

value: Payments network for Latin America that lets banks, fintechs and large platforms offer bill payments, cash in and out, mobile top-ups and gift cards through a single integration.

tapi sells a single API to fintechs, banks and retailers (clients named include Nubank, Mercado Pago, Santander and OXXO) covering bill payments, airtime top-ups, digital gift cards and cash transactions across five countries. It reports more than 250 million transactions a year, over 20,000 service companies and 70,000 physical points, and says it reached profitability in 2025. Mexico is now its largest market, and it bought Mastercard's Arcus units there.
note: LatamFintech, 2026-02-04. Paraphrased; figures are the company's.

value: Brazilian antifraud platform that uses machine learning to block fraudulent e-commerce purchases while approving legitimate ones, reducing chargebacks.

Legiti connected to a merchant's site or app through an API, collected user behaviour data and scored each transaction with a predictive model of over 3,000 features. Clients, mostly delivery and e-commerce companies, paid a monthly fee per analysed transaction. In its early case study with a pet-products delivery app it reported a 64% drop in chargebacks.
note: Brazil Journal, 2020-11-30. Paraphrased; results are the company's.
Our label; the product is antifraud scoring for online merchants.
